system.notes:
Armed helicopter — a variant of the standard Wasp with Ares Armorflex vehicle armour.

Armament: one Light Machine Gun under the nose, 100 rounds (Belt, internal), Laser Sight, rigged for automatic 6 shots with no Recoil Modifier.

Pilot: QE p.16 says "use the Knight Errant Security Guard above, but substitute Rotor for Car at the same value" — so the p.19 block with Rotor 3. That is a note, not a separate actor.

Conversion: chassis by method A from the 42B; Armor 1 → 3 by the ×3 rule, which applies here and only here; the LMG by method A (7S). Method B would have given 8S — recorded in the audit as the one weapon where the two methods disagree.

A single-seat police/military light rotorcraft.

Cruising speed 65 m/CT (used for vehicle tests). Max speed 130 m/CT. Stats: SR2E p.264-265.

Stats verified against the Rigger 2 Vehicle List (SR2, book p.148+). Northrup Wasp (PRC-42B variant).

Light machine gun, belt-fed 50 (c). Popular with merc units worldwide; the most common LMG model. Has a hip-brace recoil pad (Rating 1) and an ammunition bin slung over the shoulder. The only entry the book's Light Machine Guns section lists — there is no generic LMG. Light Machine Guns is a FIREARMS concentration (p.70); Gunnery governs heavy weapons "on tripods, vehicle mounts, pintles, or in fixed emplacements", so a VEHICLE-MOUNTED Valiant is fired with Gunnery even though the weapon itself is a firearm. SR2E p.238, p.255.

Queen Euphoria conversion (core p.283, method A — substitute the SR2 item). Printed SR1 code: 5S3. The PRC-42D's nose gun (p.16). NOTE: methods disagree here — A gives 7S, B gives 8S. A wins on p.283's preference ordering. Re-check if the mislabelled Light_Machine_Gun_Generic file in the system pack resolves to a different weapon.
